title: Creole verbs and times of day: sleep, get up, French, morning
summary: Allen asks for verbs and words like couche, arrive, Francais, Creole and matin.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers

blocks.x: All right, Judy, it's ready. If you've got any more things. Well, if you can just think of some verbs. Can you think of some, like, see, we did run, didn't we? What are some of the different things you do? Well, we've done eat. We've got eat on there. What do you say when you go to bed?
Going is the only way I say it.
Arrive. Get up out of bed?
Now you're going to say, mostly, arrive. Arrive.
I say, I say arrive again.
What is the word for Creole?
That's the only way I know it. I mix it up. I say arrive instead of arise.
No, but how do you say French? French in French. The word French.
I see. It's like the English word, but with a different pronunciation.
How about when you get up in the morning? Get up. He gave you that, didn't he? No, he said arrive.
You use that for get up? That's the same. You use the same.
See you. See you. See you. See you. My time this morning. Love you all yesterday. You're on the lead today.
